newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE arms show denies participation to Israel.
newsitem.headline: UAE arms show denies participation to Israel.

text.p: The Middle East's biggest arms show, which starts in Abu Dhabi on Sunday, turned down Israeli applications to participate, an exhibition official said on Saturday.

Brigadier Sultan al-Suweidi, organising committee chairman of the International Defence Exhibition and Conference (IDEX), told reporters several Israeli companies had applied for stands to present their wares during the five-day exhibition.
"We do not have any kind of connections with Israel and so we rejected their applications," he said.
Suweidi said organisers had also turned down Iranian applications for stands but had invited Tehran to send a delegation to the opening ceremony.
"Iran applied too late so we couldn't accept the application," he said.
He said he did not know if Iran would send a military or civilian delegation to the ceremony, how many people would attend, or if they would stay for the exhibition.

For years Iran and the United Arab Emirates have been locked in a dispute over three Gulf islands claimed by both states. The islands of Abu Musa, the Greater and Lesser Tunbs lie close to major shipping lanes in the Gulf.
Suweidi said the UAE would announce several deals at the show but did not give any details.
Some 700 international companies will participate in IDEX, which is sponsored by the UAE's armed forces.
Companies include big players such as France's Dassault Aviation and Lockheed Martin Corp of the United States, but smaller firms from countries like Egypt, Turkey and Bulgaria will also participate.
